content.text:
I found a second crash, fixed it, and tested the fix on your Minecraft without shaders. Your balloon now works.

## The second crash
Your crash report from Oct 22, 22:01 was on 10.22, the version with the first fix. 10.22 still crashed the **game client** as soon as a lit balloon came into view. The code that draws the hot-air effect inside the envelope prepared its data in the wrong order: it wrote to graphics memory while a drawing step was still open, and Minecraft 1.21.11 throws an error when that happens. Shaders don't matter: I got the same crash on plain Minecraft and on Sodium without Iris. Our tests missed it because their test ship had a burner with no envelope above it, so a balloon never formed.

## The fix
- **Code:** the balloon renderer now prepares everything before it starts drawing. The changes are in `ClientBalloonEffectRenderer` and `HeatedCulledRenderRegion`.
- **Test:** the flight test scene now builds a lit balloon. It crashed before the fix and passes after, on both plain Minecraft and Sodium.
- **New jar:** `aeronautics-fabric-1.21.11-1.3.2+mc1.21.11-port.2.jar`. My code scan on it comes back clean.
- **Pushed** as branch `fix/balloon-render-pass` (commit `20d66c8`). I haven't merged it into main or made a release.

## Test on your Minecraft
I launched your TLauncher install, the same mods you play with plus the fixed jars, from a separate game folder with Iris shaders off. It joined a local server running a copy of your server world. As player `Tester` it:
1. Built and lit a balloon on your terrain; the balloon filled and rendered.
2. Turned it into a ship, which flew up to about y 186 and levelled off.
3. Saw the server restart: the client disconnected cleanly, and the ship reloaded in mid-air.
4. Rejoined next to the floating ship and rendered it with no crash.

## Still open
- **Shaders on:** not tested yet. Your Oct 22 crash happened with shaders on, and the effect also runs during Iris's shadow pass. I'd test that before telling friends to use shaders.
- **Right-click blocks:** the physics assembler and other right-click blocks need a person to use them.
- **Your call:**
  - **Release:** whether to publish a release with the port.2 jar.
  - **Friends' server:** whether to bring Aeronautics back there, which means removing the retired prefixes in `mods.json` and pointing everyone at the new jar.
- **Test-check false alarm:** our remap-safety test flags Sable's sound methods, but the release jars are fine. I noted it in `PROGRESS.md`.

The test server and your test client are still running if you want to fly it yourself (`Tester` is in creative). Your normal install and the world archive are untouched. When you're done, close the game window and I'll stop the server; the world copy in scratch takes about 8 GB and I can delete it.

content.text:
I haven't confirmed that everything about flying works yet. So far your Minecraft has rendered a heated balloon without crashing and a test ship has flown. Driving a ship yourself with propellers, throttles and the wheel is what we're about to test.

The mini ship is built on the water next to your friend's ship, and you're standing on its deck:
- **Deck:** 9 × 5 planks.
- **Lift:** a propeller bearing with a 3 × 3 sail rotor, run through a throttle.
- **Forward:** a stern wooden propeller, run through its own throttle.
- **Steering:** a steering wheel at the bow, wired through a gearbox to a sideways propeller.

What I've checked so far, before launch:
- **Throttles:** both control their rotors. You moved them earlier (they went from 15 to 1 and 5) and the rotor speeds followed, from 0 up to 224 and 160 RPM. They're closed again now, so the ship will float first.
- **Steering:** the wheel and side propeller are idle. That's normal until someone holds the wheel, so your first turn is the real test.

**Next step is yours:** hold right-click on the Physics Assembler in front of you. I'm watching the server and will report the ship's position and speed once it assembles. Then try the lift throttle, the forward throttle and the wheel.

A few things to know:
- **Your friend's big ship isn't flying.** It's still ordinary blocks. I added a plank deck, four rotors and glue on top of it, all on this test copy only. You switched to the mini ship before it could be assembled. I found two limits along the way:
  - The `/sable assemble connected` command counts water as part of the ship, so it can't lift a ship that sits in the sea. The in-game Physics Assembler doesn't have this problem.
  - The Physics Assembler only uses honey glue whose centre is within 48 blocks of it, so a very long ship needs several glue patches.
- **A Create deployer couldn't right-click the assembler, or even a lever, on this server.** I didn't dig into why.
- **Nothing here touches your real world.** It's all on the scratch copy. Your real install and the world archive haven't been changed.

content.text:
I found what happened, from the blocks left behind and the dropped items:

1. **Launch worked.** You assembled the mini ship at 15:10:04. It floated at the waterline (y 63.3, mass 34), and none of the rotors were spinning yet.
2. **It moved and tipped.** In about 40 seconds it travelled roughly 7 blocks toward the stern corner of your friend's ship. It also turned about 90° and rolled, sinking a little (y 60.2, falling at 2 blocks/s). That fits a top-heavy design: a single plank layer with the motor, transmission, bearing and sail rotor stacked three blocks high in the middle.
3. **Then it came apart, at 15:10:46.** The ship stopped being a physics ship. Its sail rotor was put back as normal blocks at (117–119, 63, 10–12), right against your friend's hull. Most other parts (throttles, motors, wheel and so on) are floating around as **dropped items**; they all dropped at the same moment. That's what a Physics Assembler disassembly does when the ship is tilted and overlapping other blocks: anything that can't be placed back on the grid drops as an item. My guess is the assembler got right-clicked a second time. Did you click it again, or break something?
4. **The steering propeller never left.** It's still at its build spot (126, 63, 19), so it wasn't part of the ship. Steering wouldn't have worked on this build.
5. **Nothing crashed.** Neither the game nor the server had an error through the whole ride.

What I'd change for a second mini ship:
- **Stability:** a 2-layer hull that's wider than it is tall, with the lift rotor sitting low.
- **Space:** build it in open water well away from your friend's ship.
- **Side propeller:** fix it so it's actually attached to the ship.
- **Seat:** add a seat by the wheel, so you're carried along steadily while steering.

Should I rebuild it that way?

content.text:
I built the new mini ship on the water where you were hovering. You're standing on its deck next to the Physics Assembler. All the parts placed cleanly, both motors drive their transmissions, and the throttles are closed, so it will just float until you push them.

**How to fly it.** The bow points east, toward the steering wheel; the stern is west, where the rear propeller is.

1. **Launch:** hold right-click on the Physics Assembler in front of you, **once**. It should settle and float. Clicking it again later turns the ship back into blocks. That's probably what broke the last one apart.
2. **Sit:** use the seat behind the steering wheel.
3. **Up and down:** use the **lift throttle** on the deck, under the sail rotor on its stern side. Hold right-click and push it to rise, ease it back to hover or sink. The rotor is strong, so go slowly; hover is a little past halfway.
4. **Forward:** use the **forward throttle** by the rear propeller. I reversed its motor because the last ship went backwards. If it still goes backwards, tell me and I'll flip it.
5. **Steering:** hold right-click on the **steering wheel** and turn it to swing the bow left or right. Let go to stop turning.
6. **Landing:** bring the lift throttle down slowly onto the water. Then click the assembler to turn the ship back into blocks.

Compared with the last one: it has a two-layer hull, the lift motor and transmission are built into the hull so the rotor sits lower, there's a seat, and the glue has extra room around every part.

I'm watching the server for the launch. When it happens I'll tell you whether every part came along, especially the side propeller that does the steering, which got left behind last time.

content.text:
The cockpit is done, and the board is readable from the seat (in your screenshot: **LEFT LEVER = LIFT**, **WHEEL = STEER**, **RIGHT LEVER = FORWARD**).

**Your cockpit,** sitting in the seat facing the board and wheel:

| Where | Control | What it does |
|---|---|---|
| In front of you | **Steering wheel** | Hold right-click and turn left or right to swing the ship's nose that way. Let go to go straight. |
| On your left post | **Lift lever** | Push to rise, pull back to sink. Half pushed gives about half power. |
| On your right post | **Forward lever** | Push to go forward, pull back to stop. |
| Just behind you, left side | **Physics Assembler** | Click once to launch, once more after landing to turn the ship back into blocks. |
| Sign board, above and around the wheel | **Instructions** | Top row: what each control does. Bottom row: start and land steps (partly behind the wheel). |

**To fly:**
1. Right-click the **Physics Assembler** once. The ship becomes a physics ship and floats on the water.
2. Sit in the **seat**.
3. Push the **left lever** a little at a time until it rises, then ease it back toward the middle to hold height. The rotor is strong, so go slowly.
4. Push the **right lever** to go forward.
5. Hold the **wheel** and turn to steer.
6. To land, bring the left lever back slowly so it settles on the water, then click the assembler.

I tested both levers before launch: the left lever spins the lift rotor (half gives 112 RPM, closed gives 0), and the right lever spins the rear propeller (open gives 256). The steering and the forward direction can only be tested once you're flying. If forward pushes you backwards, or the wheel doesn't turn the ship, tell me and I'll fix it.

Two notes:
- **Levers start fully pulled back (off).** That's why nothing moves until you push them.
- **The lift rotor already picked up its sails** while I was testing, so it shows up as a separate spinning part. That's normal; the last ship took its rotor along the same way.

I'm still watching the server and will tell you once the ship launches and whether everything came along.

content.text:
The ship goes down because I wired the lift motor backwards. It drives the rotor through two cogwheels meshing together, and that reverses the direction, so pushing the lift lever pushed the ship down instead of up.

I flipped the motor, but you re-launched just before my change landed, so the ship in the water still has the old backwards motor. I removed the leftover copy of my fix that was floating in the water.

**To fix it:**
1. Pull the **left lever** all the way back.
2. Let the ship settle on the water.
3. Click the **Physics Assembler** once to turn it back into blocks.
4. **Wait** for a green **"Fixed! Click the assembler ONCE to launch again"** message on your screen. It appears a few seconds after the ship turns into blocks; I'm watching for that moment to flip the lift motor.
5. Click the assembler once to launch, sit down, and push the left lever slowly. It should rise now.

The rest of the ship is fine. The side steering propeller came along when it turned back into blocks, so steering should work once you're in the air. If the right lever pushes you backwards, tell me and I'll flip that motor too.

content.text:
The crash was in the server, not your game, and it's a real bug in our port that would also have hit your friends' server. I fixed it, rebuilt the flying boat, and restarted your game onto its deck.

**Why it crashed:** the Physics Assembler couldn't turn the tilted ship back into blocks. The code meant to show you a "couldn't align" message instead used a text helper that only exists in the game client. A server can't load client-only code, so the whole server went down. On your friends' server, anyone landing a tilted ship would have taken the server down the same way.

**The fix:**
- **Server text:** that message, and four other server-side messages with the same problem, now build their text without the client-only helper.
- **Wider check:** I scanned every server-side class in the three mods for other calls into client-only code and found nothing else that would run on a server.
- **Pushed:** the new Simulated jar (`…-port.1`) is installed on the test server and your test client, and the fix is pushed to branch `fix/balloon-render-pass` (commit `1976a65`).

**The new boat:** same mini design as before, and checked before you joined:
- **Lift:** the lift motor runs the right way now. Half lift spins the rotor at −112, the direction that lifted our test ship; the broken one was +112.
- **Levers:** both start pulled fully back (off) and are on wireless links beside the seat.
- **Sign board:** at the front explains each control.

**How to fly:**
1. Right-click the **Physics Assembler** once. It's just behind you, on your left.
2. Sit in the **seat**, facing the wheel and board.
3. Push the **left lever** slowly until you rise. Ease it back toward the middle to hover.
4. Push the **right lever** to go forward.
5. Hold the **wheel** and turn to steer.
6. To land, bring the left lever back slowly. Only click the assembler when the boat is **level and resting on the water**; if it's tilted it refuses now instead of crashing.

Nothing has been tested in flight yet: forward and steering only show once you're up. If the right lever moves you backwards or the wheel doesn't turn the boat, tell me. I'm watching the boat's height and speed once you launch.

Your usage limit has been reached, so I have to stop here. I haven't built the new non-flipping boat yet.

**What's done:**
- **Three real crashes found and fixed, all pushed** to branch `fix/balloon-render-pass`:
  - The balloon burner crashed the server in 10.18 (already fixed in 10.22).
  - Seeing a lit balloon crashed the game client.
  - Landing a tilted ship crashed the server.
- **Old test builds removed:** the balloon test ship, everything I'd added to your friend's ship (it's back to how they built it), and the first mini ship's leftovers. Your world's own force-loaded chunks were cleared by my cleanup and then restored.
- **Flip v3 and test ship A removed.** Test ship B (twin rotors) is still sitting on the ground at about (90, 66, 30), since it dropped when its rotors failed to start.
- **Notes:** added the findings to `PROGRESS.md`, not committed.

**What I learned about the flipping:**
- **It isn't width alone.** v3 had a gyro bearing, a 7-wide hull and a stone keel, and it still flipped once you pushed the lift.
- **The boats were underpowered.** One 3×3 rotor at full power (1,382 thrust) barely beats the weight of a 7-wide hull (about 110 × gravity 11 ≈ 1,215). You have to push the lever hard, and that's when they tip.
- **With too little lift it doesn't flip.** It just sits in the water, leaning about 8°.

**What's left:**
1. **Testing method:** my mid-air tests didn't work. After `/sable assemble area` the rotors never start, and I can't move the levers on a flying ship by command, because its blocks live in Sable's own plot files rather than the normal world. That needs solving before I can prove a design doesn't flip without you at the controls.
2. **New boat by you:** with that sorted, build the new version where you are. It would have two counter-rotating gyro rotors with bigger sails, which is your idea and the most likely fix, and enough lift to rise at about half lever.
3. **Your friends' server:** release the fixed jars there (`aeronautics port.2`, `simulated port.1`), once you decide.

import sys

c = []

c.append(f"setblock {P(5,1,0)} create:cogwheel[axis=y]")
c.append(f"setblock {P(5,2,0)} aeronautics:gyroscopic_propeller_bearing[facing=up]")
c.append(f"fill {P(4,3,-1)} {P(6,3,1)} create:white_sail[facing=up]")
c.append(f"fill {P(3,3,0)} {P(7,3,0)} create:white_sail[facing=up]")
c.append(f"fill {P(5,3,-2)} {P(5,3,2)} create:white_sail[facing=up]")
c.append(f"setblock {P(5,3,0)} minecraft:oak_planks")

c.append(f"setblock {P(6,0,0)} minecraft:stone")
c.append(f"setblock {P(6,1,0)} minecraft:stone")
c.append(f"setblock {P(7,1,0)} minecraft:stone")
# forward: stern drive on the deck, propeller behind the stern
c.append(f"setblock {P(1,2,-1)} create:creative_motor[facing=west]{{ScrollValue:-256}}")
c.append(f"setblock {P(0,2,-1)} simulated:analog_transmission[axis=x]")
c.append(f"setblock {P(0,2,0)} create:cogwheel[axis=x]")
c.append(f"setblock {P(-1,2,0)} aeronautics:wooden_propeller[facing=west]")
c.append(f"setblock {P(0,3,-1)} create:redstone_link[facing=up,receiver=true]{F}")
# steering: wheel at the bow, gearbox below, shafts to a side propeller
c.append(f"setblock {P(9,1,0)} create:gearbox[axis=x]")
c.append(f"fill {P(9,1,1)} {P(9,1,4)} create:shaft[axis=z]")
c.append(f"setblock {P(9,1,5)} aeronautics:andesite_propeller[facing=south]")
c.append(f"setblock {P(9,2,0)} simulated:steering_wheel[facing=west,on_floor=true]")
c.append(f"setblock {P(8,2,0)} create:white_seat")
# levers on posts beside the seat, wireless transmitters on the posts' inner faces
for dz, freq, name in ((-1, L, "lift"), (1, F, "fwd")):
    c.append(f"setblock {P(8,2,dz)} minecraft:oak_planks")
    c.append(f"setblock {P(8,3,dz)} simulated:throttle_lever[face=floor,facing=east,inverted=true]{{State:15}}")
    c.append(f"setblock {P(7,2,dz)} create:redstone_link[facing=west,receiver=false]{freq}")
    c.append(f"setblock {P(6,2,dz)} minecraft:stone")
    c.append(f"setblock {P(6,2,dz)} minecraft:air")
    c.append(f"#{name} {P(8,3,dz)}")
c.append(f"setblock {P(7,2,-2)} simulated:physics_assembler[face=floor,facing=north]")
c.append(f"#assembler {P(7,2,-2)}")
# sign board on a wall at the bow
c.append(f"fill {P(10,2,-1)} {P(10,3,1)} minecraft:oak_planks")
signs = {(3,-1): ["LEFT LEVER","= LIFT","push: go UP","pull: go DOWN"], (3,0): ["WHEEL = STEER","hold right-click","turn left/right","release: straight"],
         (3,1): ["RIGHT LEVER","= FORWARD","push: faster","pull: stop"], (2,-1): ["1. START","right-click the","assembler ONCE","(on your left)"],
         (2,1): ["LAND","lift lever down","slowly, settle","level, assembler"]}
for (dy, dz), lines in signs.items():
    msg = ",".join(f'"{t}"' for t in lines)
    c.append(f"setblock {P(9,dy,dz)} minecraft:oak_wall_sign[facing=west]{{front_text:{{messages:[{msg}]}}}}")
for bx, by, bz in ballast:
    c.append(f"setblock {P(bx,by,bz)} minecraft:stone")
# glue: hull + deck gear (rotor layer has its own), the bow wall
c.append(f"summon create:super_glue {P(5,0,0)} {{Box:[-6.5d,0.0d,-4.5d,5.5d,3.0d,5.5d]}}")
c.append(f"summon create:super_glue {P(5,3,0)} {{Box:[-2.5d,0.0d,-2.5d,2.5d,1.0d,2.5d]}}")
c.append(f"summon create:super_glue {P(10,2,0)} {{Box:[-0.5d,0.0d,-1.5d,0.5d,2.0d,1.5d]}}")
print("\n".join(c))
EOF

content.text:
I can't read your assembled ship's blocks directly yet: Sable keeps them in its own plot storage format, and decoding that takes a while. But the save already answers the main question. Your world has **"Head in the Clouds"** unlocked. The game only awards that once a balloon actually forms over a burner and fills with hot air. So **the balloon code is working**: no crash, no error in the log, the burner finds the envelope and fills it. Most likely it just isn't making enough lift for the weight it's carrying.

**How lift works in this mod:**
- **Lift:** each cubic metre of hot air lifts **1.5** units of mass.
- **Burner output:** one burner puts out at most **500 m³**, and only with a **full-strength redstone signal (15)** and its hot-air setting scrolled to the maximum (500). With a weaker signal or a lower setting it puts out proportionally less.
- **Balloon size:** a balloon holds no more hot air than the space inside the envelope. A 5×5×4 inside space holds 100 m³, which lifts only 150, however many burners you add.
- **Ship weight:** planks and logs weigh 0.5 each, most other blocks (stone, machines, ores) 1.0, envelope blocks 0.25.
- **Example:** a 9×5 plank deck with two layers is about 45 already. Add envelope, machinery and gear and you quickly need hundreds of m³ of hot air.
- **Fill time:** a balloon fills gradually, taking roughly 10–20 seconds to get near full. Your game is also lagging (`Can't keep up! 78 ticks behind`), which slows that further.

**Things to check, roughly in order:**
1. **Goggles on the burner:** wear the Aviator's Goggles (you have the recipe) and look at the burner. It shows the balloon's volume, how full it is, and how much it can lift. Compare that number with your ship's weight.
2. **Redstone:** the burner needs a full-strength signal (lever or redstone block, 15). A long redstone line or analog source gives less hot air.
3. **Hot-air setting:** scroll on the burner's value box and turn it up to 500.
4. **Bigger balloon:** if lift is below the ship's weight, make the envelope bigger (taller and wider inside) and add burners, about one burner per 500 m³ of inside space.
5. **Clear line upward:** nothing solid should sit between the burner and the envelope ceiling, or the burner won't find the balloon.
6. **Fully closed envelope:** the sides need to be sealed; only the bottom can be open.

If you'd like a definite answer instead of a checklist, tell me roughly how big the balloon is (inside size), how many burners there are, and what powers them, or put the goggles on and tell me the numbers. I can also write a reader for Sable's plot storage and list your ship's exact blocks and weight. That takes longer, but then I can tell you exactly how much balloon you need.

Separately, the boat-stability tests I was running before this found what makes the propeller boats flip: they need a **gyroscopic** propeller bearing **exactly over the centre of the hull**. I was about to build a balanced version for you.

Both repos are pushed. I skipped the final in-game test you stopped. Instead I booted a dedicated server with the full new pack (all 166 mods, including the 6 new jars) and it started with no errors. I haven't run the gameplay sweep or a client test on these exact jars.

- **Aeronautics `port.2`:** fixes the game crashing when a lit balloon is in view.
- **Simulated `port.1`:** fixes the server crashing when a tilted ship can't be turned back into blocks.
- **Sable `port.1`:** unchanged.

**Your friends' modpack repo** (`A1K2S3/minecraft`, commit `64c3894`):
- **Aeronautics is back:** Aeronautics, Sable and Create Simulated are pinned to the new release.
- **Your three mods are added,** each pinned to one version for both server and clients:
  - **Weapons Expanded** 1.9.3.1.
  - **Enchantments Expansion** v1.2.0. I used its Fabric mod version, which fits the repo better than the datapack zip.
  - **Extended Vanilla Endgame** 1.0.0.
- **Repo script:** the mod list generator can download mods from a GitHub release again, and it still removes modflared from friends' installs.

**To roll it out:**
1. On the VM: `git pull`, then `./server/restart`.
2. Every friend re-runs their installer one-liner. It picks up the new jars and replaces the old Aeronautics ones.

**Still open:**
- **Shaders:** a lit balloon with Iris shaders turned on hasn't been tested.
- **Server memory:** the VM is set to 8 GB but has only about 7.2 GB, and this update adds more mods. I'd lower the server memory to 5–6 GB before restarting.
- **Building flying boats:** use a **gyroscopic propeller bearing**, placed **exactly over the middle of the hull**. In my tests that stayed within 5° of level; anything off-centre, or a normal bearing, flipped. The test scene that showed this is still uncommitted in my scratch copy.
- **Your local `integration` branch** is behind `main`. I didn't touch it.
- **PROGRESS.md:** updated but not committed.

Your skin is now the default in your own Minecraft. I installed the CustomSkinLoader mod and set it to load your skin before checking Mojang. I tested it by launching your game as **KiraKami** and joining a server: the mod loaded your skin from the local file. The arm model is set to auto-detect, and your skin has slim arms, so it should show as slim. I didn't check that visually in game.

**Set up in:**
- **Your normal TLauncher install** (`~/Library/Application Support/minecraft`), for the names **KiraKami** and **Guardian**.
- **The test game folder** I've been using, which is running your single-player world right now. Restart that game to see it.

**Things to know:**
- **Only you see it.** This mod changes how *your* game draws you. For your friends to see the skin on the server, run once in game as Guardian: `/skin set web slim "https://namemc.com/texture/eca1f9a3e434107b.png"`
- **Someone else's cape.** A real Mojang account called "Kirakami" exists and has a cape, and since you have no cape of your own, the mod shows that player's cape on you. If you don't want it, I can turn capes off.
- **Only this setup.** It covers 1.21.11 in this install. Another Minecraft version or install needs the mod added there too. TLauncher's own skin upload (on tlauncher.org) would cover every version but needs your login.
- **Changing it later:** replace `KiraKami.png` / `Guardian.png` in `CustomSkinLoader/LocalSkin/skins/` inside the Minecraft folder.

content.text:
That error was my fault: the link I gave you is served as a generic file (`application/octet-stream`), and SkinRestorer only accepts links served as images. This one works:

```
/skin set web slim "https://s.namemc.com/i/eca1f9a3e434107b.png"
```

It's the same skin, identical pixel for pixel; it's just stored in a more compact PNG format. A server can download it and gets it back as `image/png`, which is what SkinRestorer checks for. Use it the same way as before: as Guardian on your friends' server, or in any world that has SkinRestorer.
